title: Two Clocks for Pressure
endLine: A fast reflex shrinks pressure errors; slow salt balance sets the level.

scenes.tts: All day, posture and activity push your arterial pressure around. Within seconds, a reflex pushes back, but it never quite finishes. So what decides where pressure settles?
scenes.narration: All day, posture and activity push your arterial pressure around. Within seconds, a reflex pushes back, but it never quite finishes. So what decides where pressure settles?
scenes.caption: All day, posture and activity push your arterial pressure around. Within seconds, a reflex pushes back, but it never quite finishes. So what decides where pressure settles?
scenes.visual: THE WORLD, built here and kept for the whole film (16:9). COLOUR BY CONCEPT, same in every scene: arterial pressure trace and pressure marker bright WHITE; the squeeze on the small arteries a RED clamp; stretch sensors and their signal CYAN; vagal output a PURPLE wire; sympathetic output ORANGE wires; blood pale BLUE fluid with drifting dots; sodium (salt) GOLD dots; the kidney's line GREEN; the salt-intake line GOLD dashed. LAYOUT: LEFT 55% of the frame is one simple circulation loop filling about 70% of frame height (schematic, no anatomy detail): a HEART pump at lower left; an ARTERY rising from it into an arch (label 'aortic arch' appears only in s03) with a side branch up to a small bulge (the carotid sinus); two small CYAN sensor rings, one on the bulge and one on the arch; a box at top left labelled 'brainstem'; a narrow tube section on the right side of the loop labelled 'small arteries'; a wider VEIN returning along the bottom to the heart. Pale blue dots flow round the loop at a pace set by the heartbeat. RIGHT 45%: a plot of mean pressure against time, y axis 95 to 125 mmHg, x axis 'seconds'; a dashed WHITE line at 100. A WHITE dot draws the live trace. Hook motion: the WHITE trace jitters and takes three short bumps up and down (schematic, unnumbered); each bump is met within a second by a CYAN flicker at the sensors and a brief pulse along the PURPLE and ORANGE wires, and each bump shrinks but does not flatten completely. On the question, white text across the top: 'Where does pressure settle?'

Title 'Two Clocks for Pressure' fades in above the plot for 2 s while the question text fades out. The trace smooths to a flat line on the dashed line at 100; the WHITE dot keeps drawing it forward. Blood dots keep flowing round the loop at the resting pace. Wires at resting brightness.

scenes.tts: An adult's mean arterial pressure at rest is about ninety-three millimeters of mercury. Call it one hundred. Squeeze the small arteries, and with no reflex, it would climb to one hundred and twenty.
scenes.narration: An adult's mean arterial pressure at rest is about 93 mmHg. Call it 100. Squeeze the small arteries, and with no reflex, it would climb to 120.
scenes.caption: An adult's mean arterial pressure at rest is about 93 mmHg. Call it 100. Squeeze the small arteries, and with no reflex, it would climb to 120.
scenes.visual: The dashed line at 100 gets the label 'start: 100 (rounded from 93)'. A tag 'teaching numbers' appears at bottom right of the plot and stays all film. On 'squeeze', a RED clamp closes on the small-arteries tube, which visibly narrows; the clamp stays closed for the REST OF THE FILM, in every scene. On 'with no reflex', the PURPLE and ORANGE wires grey out (cut, for this ghost only) and a dashed RED ghost trace rises from 100 to 120 and levels off, labelled 'no reflex: 120'. The ghost trace stays on the plot, faint, until s08.

scenes.tts: That rise of twenty is the disturbance. But stretch receptors sit in the carotid sinuses, in the neck, and in the aortic arch. They fire faster as the walls stretch.
scenes.narration: That rise of 20 is the disturbance. But stretch receptors sit in the carotid sinuses, in the neck, and in the aortic arch. They fire faster as the walls stretch.
scenes.caption: That rise of 20 is the disturbance. But stretch receptors sit in the carotid sinuses, in the neck, and in the aortic arch. They fire faster as the walls stretch.
scenes.visual: A bracket from 100 to 120 on the plot, labelled 'disturbance: 20'. The wires return to colour (reflex intact from here on). The RED clamp stays closed. The real WHITE trace now starts rising from 100. On 'carotid sinuses' the camera pushes in on the bulge (label 'carotid sinus'), then on 'aortic arch' on the arch (label 'aortic arch'). Both walls bulge outward as pressure rises; the CYAN sensor rings stretch with them and emit CYAN pulses that speed up as the walls stretch.

scenes.tts: Their signals reach the brainstem, which turns vagal output to the heart up, and sympathetic output down. The heart slows. Small arteries relax, so resistance falls. Veins relax, so less blood returns.
scenes.narration: Their signals reach the brainstem, which turns vagal output to the heart up, and sympathetic output down. The heart slows. Small arteries relax, so resistance falls. Veins relax, so less blood returns.
scenes.caption: Their signals reach the brainstem, which turns vagal output to the heart up, and sympathetic output down. The heart slows. Small arteries relax, so resistance falls. Veins relax, so less blood returns.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole loop. CYAN pulses travel up from both sensor rings to the 'brainstem' box (no nerve names on screen). The PURPLE wire from brainstem to heart thickens and brightens, label 'vagal: up'. The ORANGE wires to heart, small arteries and vein thin and dim, label 'sympathetic: down'. On 'heart slows' the heartbeat and the flow of blood dots slow. On 'small arteries relax' the small-arteries tube widens PART of the way back, but the RED clamp is still on and the tube stays narrower than at the start. On 'veins relax' the vein widens slightly and fewer dots arrive at the heart. The trace meanwhile rises only partway and bends over below the ghost.

scenes.tts: Pressure settles near one hundred and six point seven. The reflex removed thirteen point three and left six point seven. Correction divided by what is left gives a gain of two.
scenes.narration: Pressure settles near 106.7. The reflex removed 13.3 and left 6.7. Correction divided by what is left gives a gain of 2.
scenes.caption: Pressure settles near 106.7. The reflex removed 13.3 and left 6.7. Correction divided by what is left gives a gain of 2.
scenes.visual: The WHITE trace levels off at 106.7 and keeps drawing flat; label '106.7'. The disturbance bracket splits in two: the upper part, 106.7 to 120, turns CYAN and is labelled 'removed: 13.3'; the lower part, 100 to 106.7, stays WHITE and is labelled 'left: 6.7'. On 'gain of two', a fraction builds from the two pieces, '13.3 / 6.7 = 2', size 34. The circuit holds the reflex state: PURPLE wire bright (vagal up), ORANGE wires dim (sympathetic down), heart slowed, small arteries partly relaxed with the RED clamp still on, vein slightly wide, sensors firing fast.

scenes.tts: A gain of two removes two thirds of a fast disturbance. The further pressure strays, the harder the reflex pushes. So why does it stop short of one hundred?
scenes.narration: A gain of 2 removes two thirds of a fast disturbance. The further pressure strays, the harder the reflex pushes. So why does it stop short of 100?
scenes.caption: A gain of 2 removes two thirds of a fast disturbance. The further pressure strays, the harder the reflex pushes. So why does it stop short of 100?
scenes.visual: On 'two thirds', the 20 bracket shows three equal segments; two of them glow CYAN ('removed'), one stays WHITE ('left'). On 'the further pressure strays', the WHITE dot is nudged up the plot and the PURPLE wire brightens further and the ORANGE wires dim further, then the dot eases back to 106.7 and the wires return to their reflex state (vagal bright, sympathetic dim). The RED clamp stays on. On the question, white text across the top: 'Why not all the way to 100?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. The trace keeps drawing flat at 106.7; the CYAN sensors keep pulsing at their fast rate; the slowed heart keeps beating; the RED clamp stays on. No other change.

scenes.tts: Its push is proportional to the error it still sees. At one hundred, the error would be zero, and so would the push.
scenes.narration: Its push is proportional to the error it still sees. At 100, the error would be zero, and so would the push.
scenes.caption: Its push is proportional to the error it still sees. At 100, the error would be zero, and so would the push.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. A WHITE double arrow labelled 'error' spans 100 to 106.7, and a CYAN arrow labelled 'push' points down from the trace, twice the length of the error arrow. Thought experiment, shown as a dashed ghost only: a ghost dot slides down toward 100; as it falls, the error arrow and the CYAN push arrow shrink together, and the ghost wires fade to resting brightness; at 100 both arrows vanish. The ghost then fades and the real dot stays at 106.7 with both arrows at full length. The dashed RED 'no reflex' ghost trace fades out here. The RED clamp stays on.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. In Guyton's framework, the textbook account, two controllers answer two questions. The reflex decides how far pressure strays. The kidney decides where pressure ends up.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. In Guyton's framework, the textbook account, two controllers answer two questions. The reflex decides how far pressure strays. The kidney decides where pressure ends up.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. In Guyton's framework, the textbook account, two controllers answer two questions. The reflex decides how far pressure strays. The kidney decides where pressure ends up.
scenes.visual: A KIDNEY cartoon appears on the circuit, on a parallel branch off the artery upstream of the clamped small arteries, draining into the vein at lower right, with a small outlet below it. On 'how far pressure strays', the 'left: 6.7' bracket on the plot glows and the brainstem box and wires pulse once; label beside the brainstem 'how far'. On 'where pressure ends up', the kidney pulses once; label beside it 'where'. The reflex state holds everywhere: vagal bright, sympathetic dim, RED clamp on, trace flat at 106.7. A small tag at top left: 'Guyton's framework'.

scenes.tts: Switch clocks, from seconds to days. The squeeze stays on. As pressure rises, the kidney excretes more sodium, and water follows. Plotted, the kidney's line climbs with pressure.
scenes.narration: Switch clocks, from seconds to days. The squeeze stays on. As pressure rises, the kidney excretes more sodium, and water follows. Plotted, the kidney's line climbs with pressure.
scenes.caption: Switch clocks, from seconds to days. The squeeze stays on. As pressure rises, the kidney excretes more sodium, and water follows. Plotted, the kidney's line climbs with pressure.
scenes.visual: A clock icon at top of the plot turns; its label morphs 'seconds' to 'days'. The RED clamp stays on. GOLD salt dots enter the blood at the top of the loop (eating) and GOLD dots with pale blue water drops leave through the kidney outlet. The time plot transforms: the time trace collapses into a single WHITE marker on a new x axis, 'mean pressure (mmHg)', 90 to 125, sitting at 106.7, labelled 'pressure now'. A new y axis rises: 'sodium out per day', no numbers. On 'climbs with pressure' (end of the scene) a GREEN straight line draws itself upward from left to right, labelled 'kidney'. Draw it from the lesson's illustrative line: sodium out = 10 x (pressure - 85), on a y scale where 150 is about 40% of axis height; show no y numbers and no equation on screen. Tag 'teaching lines' under the plot. The circuit stays visible at left with the reflex still in its state (vagal bright, sympathetic dim).

scenes.tts: The salt you eat is a flat line, the same at every pressure. The two lines cross once. Only at that crossing does salt out equal salt in.
scenes.narration: The salt you eat is a flat line, the same at every pressure. The two lines cross once. Only at that crossing does salt out equal salt in.
scenes.caption: The salt you eat is a flat line, the same at every pressure. The two lines cross once. Only at that crossing does salt out equal salt in.
scenes.visual: A dashed GOLD horizontal line slides in at the height of 150 on the hidden scale, labelled 'salt in'. Where it meets the GREEN line, at 100 on the x axis, a ring glows, labelled 'out = in'; a faint vertical dashed line drops from it to the x axis tick '100'. At the ring, two small GOLD arrows of equal length, one in and one out, balance. The WHITE 'pressure now' marker still sits at 106.7, to the right of the ring, where the GREEN line is above the GOLD line. RED clamp still on; reflex still in its state.

scenes.tts: Above it, the body loses salt and water every day. Volume shrinks, less blood returns, and pressure falls. Lower pressure means less excretion, so each day's loss shrinks.
scenes.narration: Above it, the body loses salt and water every day. Volume shrinks, less blood returns, and pressure falls. Lower pressure means less excretion, so each day's loss shrinks.
scenes.caption: Above it, the body loses salt and water every day. Volume shrinks, less blood returns, and pressure falls. Lower pressure means less excretion, so each day's loss shrinks.
scenes.visual: At the WHITE marker (106.7), a vertical GOLD gap between the GREEN line and the GOLD line is shaded and labelled 'lose 67 per day' (mEq of sodium, from the lesson's table). In the circuit, GOLD dots and water drops stream out of the kidney faster than salt comes in; the pale blue fluid in the loop visibly thins, fewer dots reach the heart, and each beat pushes a smaller puff. The day counter ticks; the WHITE marker slides left along the x axis, stepping 106.7, then 103 ('lose 30'), then 101 ('lose 10'), the shaded gap shrinking at each step (timing schematic). As pressure falls toward 100, the reflex eases back in this model: the PURPLE wire dims and the ORANGE wires brighten toward resting, the CYAN pulses slow toward resting. The RED clamp stays on throughout.

scenes.tts: But the loss stops only at the crossing. The squeeze is still on, so the heart now pumps less. The reflex left an error; the kidney leaves none.
scenes.narration: But the loss stops only at the crossing. The squeeze is still on, so the heart now pumps less. The reflex left an error; the kidney leaves none.
scenes.caption: But the loss stops only at the crossing. The squeeze is still on, so the heart now pumps less. The reflex left an error; the kidney leaves none.
scenes.visual: The WHITE marker reaches the ring at 100; the shaded gap closes; label 'balance'. In the circuit, GOLD in and GOLD out flow at equal rates. On 'squeeze is still on', the RED clamp pulses: it is STILL closed and the small arteries are narrow, with no reflex widening left (wires at resting brightness, error zero in this model). On 'heart now pumps less', the heart beats at its starting rate but each beat pushes a smaller puff than at the start, and the fluid in the loop stays thinner than at the start. On 'left an error', a faint ghost of the 'left: 6.7' bracket flashes beside the plot; on 'leaves none', it shrinks to zero.

scenes.tts: The kidney keeps changing volume while any imbalance remains. Guyton called that an infinite gain. It is slow, but in his framework, it has the final say.
scenes.narration: The kidney keeps changing volume while any imbalance remains. Guyton called that an infinite gain. It is slow, but in his framework, it has the final say.
scenes.caption: The kidney keeps changing volume while any imbalance remains. Guyton called that an infinite gain. It is slow, but in his framework, it has the final say.
scenes.visual: Schematic demonstration on the same plot: the WHITE marker is nudged a little right of the ring, and GOLD dots drain from the circuit until it slides back to the ring; nudged a little left, GOLD dots pile into the loop (more salt in than out) until it slides back. Each return is slow (day counter ticking). Label above the ring: 'infinite gain (Guyton)'. RED clamp still on; reflex wires at resting brightness; heart pumping its smaller puffs.

scenes.tts: So the nerves answer within seconds, and the kidney answers over days. Whether the reflex also helps set the level over weeks is still argued.
scenes.narration: So the nerves answer within seconds, and the kidney answers over days. Whether the reflex also helps set the level over weeks is still argued.
scenes.caption: So the nerves answer within seconds, and the kidney answers over days. Whether the reflex also helps set the level over weeks is still argued.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world: circuit at left, renal plot at right. On 'within seconds', the brainstem, sensors and wires pulse once together and the label 'seconds' appears by them. On 'over days', the kidney, the GREEN line, the GOLD line and the ring pulse together and the label 'days' appears by them. On 'still argued', a small dashed CYAN arrow appears from the brainstem toward the kidney with a question mark beside it, labelled 'open question'. RED clamp still on; marker resting at the ring.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (blood dots circulating, GOLD salt in and out at equal rates, RED clamp still on). Large white text, centred: 'A fast reflex shrinks pressure errors; slow salt balance sets the level.'
